Measured, then documented, because this crate cannot fix it internally.

Measured with examples/crl_verify_cost.rs (release, x86-64), verifying an RSA-2048-signed CRL and looking up one serial: 1k entries / 20 KiB = 0.4 ms; 20k / 410 KiB = 7.8 ms; 100k / 2.1 MiB = 34 ms. So the bead's 'ms-scale CPU' is right, and at large-CA sizes it is tens of milliseconds of uninterruptible work stalling every other task on that executor worker.

Not fixable here: offloading means a blocking pool, every blocking pool belongs to a specific runtime, and calling one would impose a runtime on consumers who chose another -- the same objection that ruled out the block_on shape when this module was designed (shape B in async_fetcher's notes).

Fixable by the consumer with existing public API, which is what async_fetcher's module docs now say: the URL extractors are public and do no I/O, and CrlChecker/OcspChecker take owned bytes and borrow only the certificates, so the CPU half moves to a blocking pool cleanly. The docs give the measured table, name what drives the cost, give a worked tokio spawn_blocking recipe, note that implementing AsyncRevocationChecker over it is a drop-in, and say when the wrappers are still right (small CRLs, OCSP, or an executor not shared with latency-sensitive work). The example and its fixture generator are committed so the table can be re-derived. Commit 7ddf44f8.
